source: Cholera Outbreak in Senegal in 2005 Was Climate a Factor PMC3432123
processing_notes: Source states: 'Among the bordering countries of Senegal in 2005... Gambia with 214 cholera cases' - interpreted as 214 sCh cases. Deaths value of 13 drawn from JHU WHO Annual Cholera Report cross-reference confirming 214 cases and 13 deaths for 2005. CFR = 13/214 = 6.07%. Regional spillover from Senegal epidemic (31,719 cases). WHO IRIN news confirmed 'a cholera-related death in a village near the Senegalese border and three cases at main hospital in Banjul.' This is a confirmed outbreak year matching JHU baseline data - AI source provides additional academic confirmation.

source: The Point Gambia - Historian Ceesay 1869 Cholera Epidemic Bathurst
processing_notes: Source states: 'Bathurst population at the time was 5000 while 1700 died of the cholera epidemic' - interpreted as approximately 5000 population with 1700 deaths (CFR approximately 34%). Note: Wikipedia Half Die article gives alternative figure of 1162 deaths from 4000 population (CFR 29%). UK Hansard 1869 describes 'lamentable visitation of cholera at Gambia, one of the most severe upon record.' Colonial records confirm mass graves used. Most sources cite 1700 deaths consistent with The Point newspaper account. Using 1700 deaths as primary figure. 19th century historical data, confidence limited. Pandemic context: fourth cholera pandemic (1863-1875) reached West Africa via North Africa.

source: Dynamics of Cholera Epidemics from Benin to Mauritania PMC5908202

WHO AFRO surveillance bulletins 2009-2024 consistently exclude Gambia from affected countries lists. Gambia excluded from multiple major cholera analyses (2011-2020 period) confirming zero reported cases. IDSR system functional (adopted 2003, third edition 2022). 2024: 14 affected countries in AFRO not including Gambia. 2025: top 5 affected countries do not include Gambia. Cholera-free status maintained 2008-2024 based on convergent multi-source surveillance evidence. Surveillance system assessment 2025 shows operational disease reporting capacity. NOTE: JHU baseline records 3 suspected cases in 2021 (sourced from WHO Annual Cholera Report); this zero-transmission entry represents the predominant absence status with the possible exception of those 3 cases in 2021 which could not be independently confirmed via AI searches.
